$comment: Authorized compatibility deltas for 0.6.0 — the equivalence manifest's named-delta record.
An entry here is a deliberate, approved change to the browser-visible surface. It is NOT an
exclusion: no equivalence surface is relaxed by anything in this file, and
tests/lib/canonical.mjs's exclusion manifest stays empty. The five surfaces observe the audit
RESULT, and the globals below appear on none of them — which is exactly why they need naming
here rather than being caught by a diff.
Together these two entries are ONE release-level compatibility policy, to be documented as one
in CHANGELOG.md and the PR description — written once, at the end, from the finished branch,
per repository policy. They stay two commits so each is mechanically auditable.
The load-bearing distinction, and the reason this file exists: the search proved NO REPOSITORY
CONSUMER. It cannot prove no consumer. A static site can be driven from a console, an
extension, or an embedding page absent from this checkout. These are authorized decisions, not
discoveries, and neither may be described as 'nothing used it'.
CORRECTED 2026-08-27, before Task 2.7 was implemented. The previous revision of this file
over-scoped Task 2.8: it folded __APP_TEST__, the i18n/renderer wiring globals and the three
generated-data transition inputs into the fourteen-function-global delta, and claimed the end
state was DnsAudit alone. Neither the binding plan's Task 2.8 nor spec §10 authorizes that.
Those nine names have REPOSITORY CONSUMERS and no direct ESM owner yet — tools/render.test.mjs
and tools/export.test.mjs read __APP_TEST__ across 528 assertions — so removing them before
the phase that gives each a home would delete coverage rather than retire an adapter. They
stay behind marked adapters and retire on their owners' schedule, recorded below rather than
silently folded into a compatibility entry that does not cover them.

why: Spec §10 derived the facade from actual consumers rather than from what looked exportable:
analyzeDomain and checkConnectivity are the ONLY two members js/app.js calls, out of 95.
77 of the rest are used by tools/scoring.test.mjs and 4 by tools/backtest.mjs; those became
direct ESM imports in Task 2.3 and need no global. The facade is the only supported browser
deltas.authorizedBy: Spec §10, 'Three stages, in order', stage 3. Sequencing confirmed by Ian 2026-08-27.
verification: src/facade.expected.json is checked in and asserted against BOTH the source module's exports
and the built bundle's global — exactly, in both directions. This delta does not pass merely
because Task 2.7 permits the global surface to move.
The legacy window.DnsAudit assignment is removed in the SAME commit that enables globalName:
an early globalName would emit a top-level var that overwrites the real object, which is the
Five-surface equivalence must stay clean through the commit.
instrumentConsequence: The contracted global is esbuild's export namespace: non-configurable accessors, and NOT the
engine object src/main.js calls. Measured — the assignment throws, and the artifact contains
the string window.DnsAudit zero times. The equivalence runner captured the RESULT surface by
wrapping window.DnsAudit.analyzeDomain, so this commit must also rebuild the oracle to the
two-execution shape spec 1.4 §8 now specifies: the facade for the result, the real UI
controls for the other four, one deterministic case, cross-surface binding asserted. No
exclusion is added and no surface is relaxed.

globalCount.note: The NAME set is unchanged; DnsAudit's membership contracts from 95 to 2. The producer moves from src/main.js to esbuild's generated boundary, so the source graph creates 23 and the bundle 24.

deltas.summary: The 14 unsupported js/app.js function globals are removed. Nothing else.
why: index.html contains no inline event handlers — the CSP carries no 'unsafe-inline', so it
cannot — and its single textual match for cancelAudit is data-i18n="btn.cancelAudit", a
locale key. Nothing in index.html, tools/ or the suites reads any of the 14.
package.json declares no main, exports or files, so this project publishes no documented
JavaScript API. The names are unsupported legacy surface, not compatibility API.
deltas.authorizedBy: Spec §10, 'The 14 function globals have no repository consumer'. Scope confirmed as these fourteen only, 2026-08-27.
verification: tests/build/parity.test.mjs asserts the artifact's global set is exactly the ten names
below — the facade plus the nine adapters that have not reached their owners yet.
Five-surface equivalence must stay clean, which requires the equivalence runner to drive the
application through real DOM events rather than through window.startAudit().

globalCount.note: NOT DnsAudit alone. The previous revision of this file said so and it was wrong: the nine names beside the facade have repository consumers and no ESM owner yet. They are marked adapters, not compatibility API, and their removal is adapter retirement rather than a compatibility delta.

knownConsequence: tests/lib/subject.mjs drives the app by calling win.startAudit(), win.exportCSV() and
win.exportHTML(). All three disappear here. The runner must dispatch real click events on
#auditBtn, #exportCsvBtn and #exportHtmlBtn instead, which needs tools/lib/dom-shim.mjs to
actually dispatch to its stored listeners — it records them today and its click() is a
no-op. That is a more faithful driver, not a workaround: a user clicks a button.
It lands in the SAME commit as the removals. No commit may remove startAudit, exportCSV or
exportHTML while leaving the runner red.

$comment: NOT compatibility deltas, and deliberately kept out of the two entries above.
Each of these nine globals has a repository consumer today. Removing one is finished work on
an adapter whose ESM owner now exists — not an authorized change to a supported surface — and
recording them here keeps that distinction visible instead of letting nine names ride out on
an entry written about fourteen others.

adapters, and Phase 6 asserts the count reached zero.
